name: Elastic - Advanced Hunting Techniques (Lateral Movement, Persistence, PS Remoting)
description: KQL hunting queries for advanced Stuxbot TTPs: lateral tool transfer via C:\Users\Public, registry run key persistence, and PowerShell remoting for lateral movement. These are the skills assessment hunts from Module 04.
source: CDSA Module 04: Introduction to Threat Hunting & Hunting With Elastic
notes:
=== Hunt 1: Lateral Tool Transfer to C:\Users\Public (T1570) ===
Attackers drop tools (SharpHound, payloads) to C:\Users\Public as it's world-writable.
Hunt: Sysmon Event 11 (FileCreate) for files written to that path.
  event.code:11 AND file.path:*Users\\Public*
  → Check user.name field to identify the user/account doing the transfer
  → Look for: SharpHound.exe, payload.exe, recon tools

Alternative — also check Event 1 (process creating files there):
  event.code:1 AND process.command_line:*Users\\Public*

=== Hunt 2: Registry Run Key Persistence (T1547.001) ===
Stuxbot uses registry Run keys for persistence.
Sysmon Event 13 (RegistryEvent - Value Set) captures Run key writes.
  event.code:13 AND registry.path:*\\Run*
  → Check registry.value field for persistence entry name
  → Common paths:
      HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run
      HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run
      HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunOnce
  → registry.data.strings field shows the command that will execute at logon

Alternative — also hunt Startup folder file drops:
  event.code:11 AND file.path:*Startup*

=== Hunt 3: PowerShell Remoting for Lateral Movement (T1021.006) ===
PowerShell Remoting uses WinRM (port 5985/5986). Sysmon Event 1 shows
wsmprovhost.exe (WS-Management Provider Host) spawned on the TARGET host.
  event.code:1 AND process.name:wsmprovhost.exe
  → Filter to DC1: event.code:1 AND process.name:wsmprovhost.exe AND host.hostname:DC1
  → Check winlog.user.name for the account used
  → Parent of wsmprovhost.exe = svchost.exe (normal; shows WinRM is the entry point)

Alternative — Windows logon events for WinRM:
  event.code:4624 AND winlog.event_data.LogonType:3 AND destination.port:5985

Alternative — check Network connections (Sysmon Event 3) to DC on WinRM port:
  event.code:3 AND destination.port:5985 AND host.hostname:DC1

=== Zeek Hunt Patterns ===
Track C2 IP persistence across days:
  destination.ip:<C2_IP> AND network.transport:tcp
  → Add: dns.answers.data column to spot C2 IP changes (ngrok rotates IPs)

Hunt DNS for ngrok (common C2 tunnel):
  dns.question.name:*ngrok.io*
  → Check dns.answers.data for resolved IP, then track connections to that IP

=== Field Reference for Hunting ===
  process.name           → executable name
  process.command_line   → full command line (with args)
  process.parent.name    → parent process name
  process.parent.command_line → parent command line
  process.pid            → numeric PID
  process.hash.sha256    → SHA256 of executable
  file.path              → full path of file created/modified
  file.name              → filename only
  registry.path          → full registry key path
  registry.value         → registry value name
  registry.data.strings  → registry value data (the command/payload)
  dns.question.name      → DNS query hostname
  dns.answers.data       → DNS response IPs
  source.ip              → source IP in network event
  destination.ip         → destination IP
  destination.port       → destination port
  host.hostname          → hostname of reporting agent
  winlog.user.name       → user from Windows event
  user.name              → ECS user field
